Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. content.text:
Rule 1 satisfied: 5 passing, 0 failing.

**Naming Evaluation (first priority)**

- `nextGeneration(liveCells)` — accurately describes computing the next generation from live cells. Keep.
- `keyOf`, `neighborsOf`, `liveNeighborCount`, `candidates`, `living` — all reveal intent.
- One weak spot: `candidates` is a `Map` of key→Cell whose purpose (every cell that could possibly be alive next gen — the live cells plus their neighbors) is only clear after reading the loop. And `count`/`isAlive` inside the final loop are fine but the survival/birth condition `count === 3 || (isAlive && count === 2)` encodes the four rules implicitly.

**Rule 2 (reveals intent)** — the rule condition is the least self-documenting part. Extracting it names the domain rule.

**Rule 3 (no duplication)** — `keyOf(candidate)` is recomputed, and the `[cell, ...neighborsOf(cell)]` spread allocates a fresh array per live cell. Minor, but the dedup-by-key logic is genuinely duplicated in concept between `living` (Set) and `candidates` (Map).

content.text:
All 5 green.

**APP mass after**

The changes: `+2` invocations for the extracted predicates and their two `===` comparisons, `-1` loop (removed the spread over `[cell, ...neighborsOf(cell)]`), `+1` conditional (the ternary replacing part of the compound `||`/`&&`).

| Component | Count | Mass |
|---|---|---|
| Constants | 21 | 21 |
| Bindings | 18 | 18 |
| Invocations | 18 | 36 |
| Conditionals (`if`, ternary, `\|\|`, 3× `===`) | 3 | 12 |
| Loops (map, filter, for ×3) | 5 | 25 |
| Assignments | 2 | 12 |

**Total mass: 124** — up from 120 (Δ +4).

Mass went **up**, and I kept the change anyway. That is the Rule-2-trumps-APP call: `count === 3 || (isAlive && count === 2)` is a correct but anonymous encoding of the Game of Life rules, and the reader has to decode which of the four rules each clause covers. `survives(n)` and `isBorn(n)` name them, so the survival threshold now lives in one place with a domain name — which matters because the remaining todos (Rule 3 Overpopulation, block still life, blinker) all exercise exactly those thresholds. Four mass units for that is worth it.

Note on the extraction's honesty: `survives` returns true for 2 or 3 neighbors, which folds Rule 1 (underpopulation, <2 dies) and Rule 3 (overpopulation, >3 dies) into a single positive predicate rather than expressing them as separate death rules. That is a deliberate simplification — the tests only ever observe the surviving set — but if you want the four canonical rules to appear one-for-one in the code, this extraction is the wrong shape and should be revisited when the Rule 3 Overpopulation test goes red.

**One thing to flag:** my first attempt replaced the loop with a `filter().map()` chain that called `liveNeighborCount(cell)` in both ternary branches — duplicated work and worse readability. I caught it on review and reverted to the explicit loop, hoisting the count into a `liveNeighbors` binding computed once. The version on disk is the corrected one; the intermediate was green but was not an improvement.

**Not changed, and why:**
- `keyOf`/`neighborsOf` — already minimal and well-named.
- The `Set` (`living`) plus `Map` (`candidates`) pair looks like duplicated dedup logic, but they hold different things (membership of the current generation vs. the candidate cells for the next), so collapsing them would conflate two concepts. Left alone.
- The `${x},${y}` string key is the standard sparse-set encoding here; no negative-coordinate hazard, since the negative-coords todo will confirm it.
